name: Marek Nowicki (synthetic)

facts.label: oversee construction project
facts.story: Plans pours and formwork with the foremen on concrete-frame housing and office projects.

facts.label: monitor construction site

answers.recent_work: For the last eleven years I've been a site engineer and later site manager on concrete-frame housing and office projects around Espoo and Helsinki. Day to day I plan the pours and the formwork with the foremen, check the drawings against what's built, and keep the quality documents in order. I'm 53, and I came from Poland in 2008 to supervise the concrete on a bridge project, and then I stayed.
answers.example: On one housing block the drawings for the stairwell did not match the structural drawings, so the openings were in different places. I found it when I overlaid the two sets before the formwork went up, called the designers the same day, and we agreed a corrected opening. Because we caught it before pouring, nobody had to break out concrete.
answers.tools: Revit and AutoCAD for reading the models and drawings, a tablet on site for the drawings and photos, and Excel for the pour schedules. I know the Finnish building code well and I fill in the inspection documents myself. Total station, level and laser for checking positions.
answers.people: I lead a crew of about twenty-five on site: the foremen, formwork carpenters and rebar fitters, plus subcontractors for electrical and ventilation. I report to the project manager and talk with the client's supervisor every week. My part is the schedule and the quality, not the budget.
answers.beyond: I started as a carpenter in my twenties, so I can read what the crew is doing. I also hold the site safety qualification and I run the safety walk every Monday. I've trained two young engineers to become supervisors.
answers.open_floor: I've worked with crews in four languages on one site, so I'm used to making sure that everyone understood the plan.
answers.looking_for: Site manager or construction supervisor job on larger projects. English and Finnish both work for me. On site, naturally. I could start in January.

probes: The overlay was done in the model viewer: I laid the structural model over the architect's one and flicked between them level by level. The stairwell openings were about ten centimetres out. I took screenshots, sent them with the drawing numbers to both designers, and asked them to confirm which one was right.

For the Monday safety walk I go around with the foremen and we list what we see on a sheet, like missing edge protection or loose material. Each item gets a person and a day, and I check on Friday that they are closed.
